newsitem.title: USA: Storm causes New England floods, one killed.
newsitem.headline: Storm causes New England floods, one killed.

text.p: A violent storm blamed for the death of a child in New York continued to pound New England on Sunday, leaving thousands without power, flooding roads and homes and tearing boats from their moorings.
Officials declared a state of emergency in several north shore Massachusetts towns, evacuating residents of low-lying areas.
A 12-year-old boy in Babylon, New York, on Long Island was killed on Saturday when a tree uprooted by strong winds toppled onto him as the storm swept through the New York area.

The National Weather Service reported wind gusts of 62 mph (100 km) in the Boston area late on Saturday afternoon. More than 6 inches (15 cm) of rain fell in parts of Massachusetts and the rain and high winds were expected to continue through the evening.
Scattered power outages continued to plague much of New England throughout Sunday.
The Weather Service issued a flood warning for north central Connecticut, where more than 3 inches (7.6 cm) of rain had fallen by early Sunday across Hartford and Tolland counties.
A flood watch was also in effect for Rhode Island, Massachusetts, southern New Hampshire, and Maine as rain continued to pound the region.

"We've had no reports of flash flooding yet, but one of the greatest threats to Massachusetts in weather like this is flash flooding," said Peter LaPorte, director of the state's emergency management agency.

The severe weather caused officials to cancel Boston's Head of the Charles rowing competition, the world's largest. Officials said the weather and "very real worries of hypothermia and increasingly bad weather" caused the cancellation. Some 4,500 atheletes had assembled for the race. It was the first cancellation in the race's 32 years.

The region's utilities, Boston Edison, Commonwealth Electric and Eastern Utilities, all reported scattered power cuts with no more than 2,000 customers in each of their service areas covering Rhode Island and Massachusetts being affected.
Connecticut residents were not so lucky and about 56,000 customers were without power there. Northeast Utilities said it hoped to have power restored to those customers by early Monday.
In New York and New Jersey, many of the 100,000 customers who lost power on Saturday continued to experience scattered outages.
The Coast Guard in Boston said a number of small sailboats had been torn from their moorings during the storm.
The National Weather Service expected 4 to 6 inches (10 to 15 cm) of rain, with up to 7 inches (17 cm) in some areas of New England before the storm was through.

The slow-moving storm on Saturday had dumped more than 8 inches (20 cm) of rain in portions of the New York City-New Jersey metropolitan area, forcing the opening game of the World Series at Yankee Stadium to be delayed until Sunday.
